title: Overexposed
subtitle: Don't worry—the guide hasn't gone anywhere.

content.text: Why would anyone else want to talk to you in riddles the same way I do?
It's kind of a chore being this vague, to be honest. He has to be getting paid for this.
Are you paid to talk to me?

branch.text: All I've received in compensation for our little talks is a dry tongue. I've already poured three pots of tea today.
Do you think you're all that interesting a conversation partner?
I'm not some retiree who has nothing else to do.
The only reason I talk to you is because you won't leave my house.
What else should I do? I'm not strong enough to throw you out.
My only defense is a razor-sharp wit, though it seems to never cut you deep enough to matter. I swear at times I think you've been glued into that chair.
*sigh* Never mind. Sometimes we just have to accept the little disappointments in life.
That old dust whines about the plaster figures intruding in his room. But that's all he's done so far.
If he wants to take over for me, do let me know. If it means not having to come up with any more riddles, I'll even let him sit in my chair.

content.text: Are you actually interested in talking to me?

items.text: Overexposed

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You are the true creator of this "boon."
And you are its rightful receiver.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Rightful receiver? Then why was it in Arcana's possession? And why was it given to Igor?
You know the ways of time and fate. The "boon" comes to you only at the proper moment, just as you have come to me.
I'm tired of riddles.

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: Perhaps on another day I would be willing to solve your riddles, but not now. I want a clear answer.
The answers you seek will come. They will find you when the sleeping mind awakens.
There is one final veil between you and the truth.

items.text: I don't know anything about time or fate.
items.edge_label: 我不知道时间和命运的秘密

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: So you say, but I've had remarkably little luck understanding either lately.
In the river of time, all creation is naught but drifting sand.
Only the weavers of the golden thread may ride upon its tides.

items.text: How do you know me?

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: You speak as though you know me. Have we met before?
Beneath the ruins of civilization, in an ancient past.
Yet neither of us came to seek that story. Not on this day.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Igor was promised that the "boon" would protect him, but it didn't. Will that happen to me as well?
The promise still stands.
But mortal hands cannot stop the sand from slipping through their fingers.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What are you expecting me to do, then?
You need no counsel from me. The "boon" is already yours.
I do not seek to bestow blessings, for you need none.
Vekiĝu en la regno de mortemuloj.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Vekiĝu en la regno de mortemuloj.
The flowing dust is blown away, revealing a familiar library, but everything appears hollow and fake, like stage dressing.
The light shines colorless and stark.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto? Where are you?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I'm right here. Can't you see me?
It is difficult to make out where Sonetto's voice is coming from.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No. I can't see anything. It's too dark.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto, where are—
A pair of surprisingly small hands grasp out and take hold of the drifting consciousness.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I'm right beside you.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: We're in the library, just us. No students, no staff, no Manus Vindictae.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: You disappeared after we went through that gate, then reappeared behind me just now.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: What do you mean you can't see? Has something happened to your eyes?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm not sure. It's like I've been hit by a flashbang. But I'll manage.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You sound different.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: That's because we're both children again. We look like we did when we were SPDM students.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Then this can't truly be reality. It's like what happened in the Amber Room.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The flow of time has been disrupted.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Where did you go after stepping into the gate, Timekeeper?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm not certain. There was a mist or dust, and I heard a voice.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It said I already knew how to gain protection from the "boon." Then it spoke an incantation.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Then, does that mean we succeeded?
Sonetto blinks. Her face is a strange mixture of joy and confusion.
It's difficult to believe things went smoothly. For her part at least, it seems as if she's been walking in circles without end.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I repeated the incantation, but I have no idea if it worked. We need to find a way out of this timeline anomaly if we're to know if it had any effect.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Speaking of time, I looked around while you were gone.
Little Sonetto can't help but feel vexed by how odd the situation is and how somehow the least troubling thing is their sudden return to childhood.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: There are no clocks, calendars, or even yearbooks in this place. Anything that might indicate a date or time is missing.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: And whenever I try to leave, I just end up back where I started. It's like a maze that won't let us go.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Wait, Sonetto.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: What is it?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There's a light, a golden thread. I can feel it, feel her.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Her?
The hand gently touches the golden thread.
An ethereal, pleasant sound trembles through the space.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's Merel.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: But I can't see her anywhere. How do you know it's her?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I just know. I can't explain how.
Far beyond what Sonetto's eyes can see, the golden thread stretches onward into the darkness until it ends tied into a knot of black nothingness.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The thread's tangled. Merel may be in trouble. But her knot isn't anywhere close.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto, where am I facing?
Following the gaze, Sonetto spies the outline of a tower looming down from a distance.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Toward the central watchtower.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I tried to find a way there earlier. But I couldn't even manage to leave the library.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let's try following Merel's thread.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Take my hand. I'll guide us. You clear the way.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Of course.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let's get out of here.
The moment the marble threshold is crossed, the mazelike space begins to collapse behind them. The library is now more than a hundred paces behind.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: We made it!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Good. Then this thread is leading us to exactly where we need to be.
The golden thread winds toward the second floor, where it ultimately tangles into another knot.
Guided by instinct, each step draws closer to the thread.
story_option_guideslide|0#0#1#9999
The knot unravels with the slightest touch.
As it does, it seems to flow across the back of the hand.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: There we go.
*click*
The sound of salvation comes from the door behind them.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Wait. It's open?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Emilia, help me open this door.
